topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the lecture series, lecturer, and the core learning outcomes relating to cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Development, Etiology, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore what defines cancer, discuss the balance between endogenous bad luck and environmental exposures, and review epidemiological studies of global cancer variation.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and the Burkitt Lymphoma Paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral and bacterial pathogens contribute to malignancy, focusing closely on the environmental and mechanistic discovery of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific environmental, dietary, and cigarette-derived mutagens—including aflatoxin, UV radiation, polycyclic hydrocarbons, and aromatic amines—undergo metabolic activation to damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, contrasting tumour initiators with promoters, detailing inflammation-driven progression, and highlighting host developmental vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Approaches for Determining and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the methodologies used to prove and evaluate carcinogenicity, from mutational signatures and human biobanks to animal models and in vitro assays.
